name: Crack a whip
blurb: The crack is a small sonic boom: the tip breaks the sound barrier. Getting one is a first-session thing; getting consistent, controlled cracks takes a fortnight.
gear: A bullwhip or stockwhip, 1.2–1.8 m for learning
Wide open space, eye protection, long sleeves
steps: Find a genuinely clear space — several whip-lengths in every direction, with nobody nearby, including behind you.
Learn the cattleman’s crack: bring the whip forward and back smoothly, then reverse direction cleanly to send a loop down the whip.
Focus on smooth acceleration and a clean direction change rather than force. Yanking it produces no crack.
Learn the overhead crack once the basic one is reliable.
Learn to control where the tip goes, which is what turns noise into a skill.
Learn basic whip care: keep it clean, conditioned, and replace the cracker when it frays.
tips: The tip can cut skin and blind an eye. Eye protection is essential and so is space.
No crack means the loop is not travelling cleanly. Slow down and smooth the motion.
proof: Ten consecutive controlled cracks with the tip landing where you intended.
